findings.evidence: template/scripts/pr_review_gate.py: `provider = "claude" if claude_binary is not None and argv[0] == claude_binary else "codex"`; the same line is in template/scripts/requirement_composition.py. bound_preflight in independent_review_runner.py instead builds a providers_by_binary map over PROVIDERS, so the three call sites resolve the provider differently.
findings.summary: The default review launchers infer the provider by comparing argv[0] to the claude binary and treat everything else as codex. The logic is duplicated in two places. A new provider in PROVIDERS, or a codex binary that resolves to the same path as claude, would silently get the codex environment and no token.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/lifecycle_workers.py read_login_token: `for parent in path.resolve().parents: if (parent / ".git").exists(): raise WorkerError(... must be outside any git checkout ...)`. The docs only say "outside any git checkout".
findings.summary: read_login_token rejects any token file with a `.git` entry in any ancestor directory. An operator whose HOME is itself a dotfiles git repo cannot keep the token anywhere under ~, and the error text does not say why. The check also tests `.git` existence only, so it does not cover a gitdir-file worktree layout in every case.

findings.evidence: pr_review_gate.py: `return subprocess_launcher(argv, cwd, timeout, env=workers.llm_env(provider, review_config or {}, home))`. By contrast, bound_preflight wraps the same call in `except WorkerError -> LaunchUnavailable`.
findings.summary: In the default review launcher in pr_review_gate.py and requirement_composition.py, llm_env can raise WorkerError for an invalid token file. This happens at launch time, after the claim, and the exception escapes the runner's LaunchUnavailable handling. A bad token file therefore fails the job with a raw exception instead of recording the reviewer as unavailable. The worker's login preflight catches it before the claim only when it is invoked through `work-next --run`.
